brief: GS's Pasquariello frames a new, more complicated phase in the AI trade for both credit and equity markets: the market is now debating both the availability and cost of capital, which triggered heavy risk reduction this week. US equities and his own long-stocks/short-bonds pairing sold off on catalysts including CPI data, higher Brent, and unrewarded ASML/TSMC earnings. AI credit spreads (GSUCHS30) widened to the year's wides while the AI leaders-vs-laggards basket gave back its entire roughly 100% YTD gain; HY continued underperforming IG and the quality-vs-low-quality equity pair (GSP1QUAL) rallied, as NDX and S&P broke down from their early-October breakout. Rates re-impinged on markets for the first time in three years, likened to SVB in 2023 and NDX in late 2023, pressuring cyclicals (RTY, BKX, CAT, VRT, GEV) despite a fine round of Q3 bank earnings. Flows showed the largest tech-selling week in a decade and cut AI stock exposure to the 35th percentile, alongside a VIX pop to 20 and record S&P put volume. He expects more month-end supply before buybacks dominate, and says Q3 earnings, starting with META on Wednesday, must restore confidence, with his base case still strength returning in November-December.
